content:
Maria (oncall): heads up — Support-Sam just flagged a customer report: p99 latency spikes to ~4.5s starting ~03:20 UTC, affecting text-generation endpoints for org: acme-inc. They say it started right after yesterday's runtime kernel update. link: https://redwood.grafana/acme/p99 (screenshot attached)

opsbot: alert: route: /v1/generate p95 1.1s -> 1.8s, p99 1.9s -> 4.6s, error_rate 0.2% (since 2026-03-15T03:18:00Z). trace_id: 0x9f3b

Support-Sam: customer on a paid Dedicated plan, says UX threads are timing out in prod browsers. They're getting 502 after 10s. Please prioritize.

Maria (oncall): quick triage: is this global or region-specific? any deploys at 03:18-03:22?

Dan (infra): checking deploys — there was a runtime patch (commit abc1234) pushed to canary at 03:10, then promoted to prod at 03:16 via rollout: 10% -> 100% by 03:25. I'll pull rollout events.

Ash (ml): fyi we merged an attention-kernel change that changed KV cache eviction heuristics. Could cause higher per-token compute if KV misses increase. Might explain p99 increase.

SRE-Lead: ok, mitigation playbook: 1) circuit-break heavy orgs to fallback model 2) apply per-org rate limit throttle 3) enable prefix/KV cache warmup 4) if needed revert runtime or force canary rollback. Start with least disruptive — circuit-break and throttle for acme-inc.

Dan (infra): I can patch routing policy via admin API. Patch below — will set fallback_model and client_rate_limit.

```
PATCH /internal/admin/routing/acme-inc
{
  "fallback_model": "redwood/gpt-small-q4",
  "client_rate_limit": {"requests_per_minute": 3000},
  "circuit_breaker": {"enabled": true, "p99_threshold_ms": 2500}
}
```

Maria (oncall): doing it now.

Maria (oncall): applied. opsbot confirmed policy apply success. Rollout id: ro-20260315-77

opsbot: policy apply: success. New routing: fallback-> redwood/gpt-small-q4, rps cap ~50 rps sustained (org-wide), circuit_breaker p99 2500ms.

Dan (infra): also temporarily increased dedicated pool burst capacity for that cluster (+2 nodes) to absorb load while fallback takes over.

Ash (ml): note — fallback model is quantized and will reduce latency but might change output quality. Inform Support-Sam and customer about degraded quality tradeoff.

Support-Sam: told customer we enabled a temporary safety mode while we investigate; they accepted.

Maria (oncall): monitoring now — initial numbers: p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 1.05s in 3 min, p99 trending down to ~1.6s. No more 502s.

opsbot: grafana snapshot: https://redwood.grafana/snapshots/abc-20260315

SRE-Lead: good. next steps: 1) reproduce locally with synthetic load and the new kernel 2) collect heap/kernel traces from affected nodes 3) consider revert if root cause confirmed. Assign owners:
- Repro + traces: Ash
- Rollback plan ready: Dan
- Customer comms and quality monitoring: Support-Sam

Ash (ml): repro in progress — running synthetic workload that mimics acme payload shape (long context + many cached prefixes). Initial run shows higher KV-miss rate after kernel change. I can correlate with commit abc1234.

Dan (infra): prepping rollback PR — if we see same in canary we revert canary then promote revert to prod. ETA 45m.

Maria (oncall): putting a temporary SLO guardrail: adding org-level automatic fallback policy for any org with p99 > 2.5s sustained for 2 minutes. Patch:

```
POST /internal/config/slo-guardrails
{
  "trigger": {"metric": "p99_latency_ms", "window": "2m", "threshold": 2500},
  "action": "enable_fallback_model",
  "fallback": "redwood/gpt-small-q4",
  "rate_limit": {"requests_per_minute": 3000}
}
```

SRE-Lead: please make sure guardrail can be safely opted-out by enterprise customers with dedicated contracts.

Opsbot: guardrail apply: queued -> success.

Maria (oncall): summary so far: mitigations applied (fallback + throttle + burst nodes), p95/p99 improving. Root cause suspected: KV cache eviction regression in kernel abc1234. Next update after Ash reproduces and Dan readies rollback.

Support-Sam: customer happy for now, will keep monitoring dashboards with me.

Ash (ml): repro confirmed. KV-miss rate increases ~3x with abc1234 under long-context workload. Creating a minimal repro gist and attaching heap traces. Suggest revert commit and re-evaluate kernel patch with additional cache tests.

SRE-Lead: prioritize revert in next 30m if safe, otherwise keep guardrails in place. Postmortem/CL will be required. Good catch team. :thumbsup:

Maria (oncall): taking action items into ticket: INF-4872, assigning Ash/Dan/Support-Sam. Will keep thread updated.
